Category: Other
Importance: 5
Female African treefrogs exhibit a unique mating behavior known as simultaneous polyandry, where they mate with multiple males to build larger foam nests that protect their eggs from drying out. Research indicates that nests constructed with the help of several males provide better chances of survival for the tadpoles, as these larger nests retain moisture and develop a hard exterior that insulates the eggs. This behavior suggests broader biological advantages for females mating with multiple partners, as seen in various species beyond treefrogs.

 - Female African treefrogs mate with multiple males to enhance the survival of their offspring.
 - The nesting-assistance hypothesis provides a new perspective on why females in many species choose multiple mates.

Global interest in holding leaders accountable for atrocities continues, even as some major governments remain hesitant to engage with the ICC.

 - The ICC is experiencing a crisis regarding its credibility and ability to deliver justice.
 - There is a growing movement among various countries to pursue accountability for international crimes independently of the ICC.
 - High-profile cases, such as that of Rodrigo Duterte, highlight the ongoing struggle for justice in the international legal system.

Source: https://foreignpolicy.com/?p=1236331
